attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his co-authored Substack post (with Davis), published under his name and endorsed. Not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: Firm 'will require' sets a necessity condition: reliable real-world agents, not demos, need common sense about objects, people and entities. Treating reliable operation as the antecedent is acceptable. No deadline was stated, and the proposition keeps the scope and the 'not just demos' qualifier.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. Reliability means consistent task completion, not perfection, and commonsense competence must be tested separately to avoid circular reasoning. Marcus gave no threshold, duration or test, so whether constrained or supervised deployments count depends on the evaluator's interpretation. That interpretation is reasonable and not stretched either way.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study of production agents from April to November 2025, available June 2026. It shows reliability is handled through tight constraints and human review. This neither establishes reliable autonomous operation nor tests commonsense competence.

Preprint from January 2026. Its simulated e-commerce tasks show strong models failing mainly on contextual inference. It is consistent with Marcus's view, but a simulation cannot establish real-world reliability or the necessity he claims.

Preprint posted October 4, 2026, before the evaluation date. It reports relative reliability gains for one deployed interviewing agent. It sets no absolute reliability standard and does not test commonsense competence, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm necessity claim with no deadline. Whether the antecedent, established reliable real-world operation, has been met is unknown. No item pairs reliable deployment with separate tests showing common sense is present or absent. The early-resolution rule, a well-documented reliable agent that lacks common sense, is not met. All three items are context only, so the evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the claim.
